name: multiple_choice: Which of the following is true of randomization in…

request.questionText: Which of the following is true of randomization in experimental design?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fundamental source of uncertainty in an experiment arises from whether or not the analysis uses bootstrapping or large-sample inference to construct a confidence interval for the treatment effect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Randomization is not necessary as long as the experimental design involves blocking.

choices.label: C
choices.text: We use randomization to identify confounders that could affect the outcome of the experiment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The goal of randomization is to construct a sample that is perfectly representative of the population.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Randomization ensures balance, on average, even for possible confounding factors of which the experimenter is not aware.
